To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of friends a youth has and the quality of his or her friendships both influence the strategies that the youth uses to help a friend or seek help from a friend.

(1) the number and quality of friendships are related to youths' strategies to help friends and (2) youths' strategies to respond to helping tasks in the fall are related to friendship quality and number in the spring.

(a) friendship quality is associated with the social strategies that children use in response to social stressors in their friendships, (b) friendship quality is also associated with the social skills that children use to help their friends when they encounter a social stressor, and (c) children who use more hostile and avoidant strategies when they are helping their friends are more likely to have fewer and lower-quality friendships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and maintenance of friendships and how friendships may be a context for the acquisition of important social skills.
the development of social competence, particularly the development of social strategies that are used in social interactions with friends.
the development of social competence and the ways in which children's social competence may influence their social relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provides important new information on how friendship adjustment and social skills may influence one another.
the quality of a person's friendships is related to their ability to respond to the social needs of friends and the social needs of themselves.
friendship provides a context for the acquisition of important skills, such as social strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of children's friendships is related to the development of their social skills, and that their social skills are related to the development and maintenance of their friendships.
friendship adjustment is a key factor that shapes social strategies, and in turn, social strategies are an important factor in shaping friendship adjustment.

friendships provide a critical context for the development and maintenance of social competencies, and that social competencies, in turn, may be important in the maintenance of high quality friendships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
friendship provides an opportunity for youths to develop social skills.
friendships may be important contexts for the development of relationship skills.
the development of social competencies and social skills is not just a matter of the child's own social skills but that it also depends upon the child's social experiences with peers.
